title: Normalized finite-free and rational direct-image squares on shifted root lines
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite intermediate extension of Q_l in its fixed algebraic closure, and f:X -> S a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes. For each DiagonalRightDerived model R of Z_l direct image there exists a RestrictionSquare [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-scalars] for integralMap with the canonical O_E model [lem-diagonal-canonical-right-derived], whose scalar mate is invertible on zlLine(l,X)[2]. For each model R of O_E direct image there similarly exists a full-unit-normalized RestrictionSquare for O_E -> E whose mate is invertible on spIntegralTwist(X,l,E)[2]. The lines and scalar maps are precisely those of [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-maps]. No class, trace, supported-source data or integration identity is part of the assertion.

proof.text: Use the existing finite integral coefficient basis at the bottom finite intermediate field. The existing base coefficient condensed identification identifies its integer ring with Z_l via exactly integralMap at the bottom field. Transport the finite point basis along this ring-object isomorphism. Pulling the basis back to each scheme proves exactness of integral scalar extension. The existing finitePush_of_pointCopower criterion, applied to this finite point basis, proves invertibility of the actual canonical derivedPushHom on every complex. Its proof only uses additivity and finite coproducts.

For any flat coefficient map, use the actual derivedComapLowerStarIso. Its full right-derived-unit equation on homotopy complexes is the existing generic square_fac calculation; convert it to the cochain-unit equation via quotientCompQhIso and exact-functor localization factors. The universal cochain units give the unique isomorphism from the canonical lower-coefficient derived model to the supplied model R. Whisker this isomorphism with restriction and compose with the actual canonical square. Naturality and the unit factorization prove precisely the RestrictionSquare normalization on every complex. The adjunction unit equation and naturality show that its mate component equals scalar extension of the inverse model comparison followed by the canonical derivedPushHom component. Hence canonical mate invertibility transports to R.

For rationalization use the exactness clause of padicIntegers_invertEll and localizedDirectImageComparison_isIso, which proves invertibility of the actual canonical derivedPushHom component on every bounded-below object. The integral Tate line single complex in degree zero shifted by two has lower bound -2, independently of the line and of invertibility of l on X. Apply the flat-square construction and transport just proved. Combine this with the integral assertion as the required conjunction; no further intermediate sorry is introduced.

lean.statement:
theorem diagonalFinite_scalarSquares
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField l)
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] :
    (∀ R : DiagonalRightDerived
        (CondensedRing.lowerStar (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} ℤ_[l]) f),
      ∃ s : RestrictionSquare (integralMap l E) f R
          (canonicalDiagonalRightDerived
            (CondensedRing.lowerStar (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj.{u} l E.1) f)),
        IsIso ((s.mate (integralMap l E)).app
          (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (zlLine l X))⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧))) ∧
    (∀ R : DiagonalRightDerived
        (CondensedRing.lowerStar (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj.{u} l E.1) f),
      ∃ s : RestrictionSquare (padicIntegersRingObjToContinuousMapRingObj l E) f R
          (canonicalDiagonalRightDerived
            (CondensedRing.lowerStar (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} E.1) f)),
        IsIso ((s.mate (padicIntegersRingObjToContinuousMapRingObj l E)).app
          (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
            (spIntegralTwist X l E))⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧)))
